paragraph: The Law Against False Information on the Internet was [published on 4 August 2026 with prison terms of up to 10 years](<https://www.novojornal.co.ao/politica/detalhe/publicada-em-diario-da-republica-a-lei-que-pune-a-disseminacao-de-informacoes-falsas-na-internet-com-ate-10-anos-de-prisao-73765.html>). In the last twelve months, on 2 October 2026, a Luanda court [sentenced Reporter Angola editor Daniel Frederico in absentia to 14 months in prison](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/law-on-false-information-on-the-internet-adopted-activists-and-journalists-detained-prosecuted/>) for slander and defamation. At the closing arguments in November 2024, [the prosecutor's side asked for three years in prison](<https://www.ecosefactos.com/jornalista-angolano-condena-tres-anos-de-prisao/>). No law repealing a speech offence has been found. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

No stage is set. On 14 September 2026 the National Communications Council [suspended a Yaga Burundi programme for six months](<https://eusee.hivos.org/alert/the-national-communications-council-suspends-programme-on-yaga-burundi-for-six-months-following-an-interview-with-a-critical-opposition-figure/>) after it aired an interview with a politician critical of the authorities. In the last twelve months, on 14 January 2026, journalist Sandra Muhoza [received a four-year prison sentence](<https://eusee.hivos.org/assets/2026/04/Burundi-2026-Snapshots-EN.pdf>) over information shared in a private press group. On 13 April 2026 the Ngozi appeal court [convicted her of 'racial aversion' with six months already served](<https://www.sosmediasburundi.org/2026/04/14/burundi-fin-dune-detention-decriee-sandra-muhoza-retrouve-la-liberte/>). Nothing found says a paper, broadcaster, party or group inside the country criticised a government policy in public. Preparing would need a source showing such criticism, with no internet cut in the past twelve months.

On 3 November 2026 [the media professionals' union UPMB and Amnesty International Bénin called for a review of articles 550 and following of the Code du numérique](<https://quotidienlexpress.bj/2026/11/04/code-du-numerique-lupmb-et-amnesty-international-benin-plaident-pour-une-relecture-des-textes/>). In the last twelve months, journalist Pascal Mitowade was [sentenced to five years in prison](<https://rsf.org/en/rsf-s-ten-recommendations-benin-s-new-president-strengthening-press-freedom>) on 24 March 2026 over Facebook posts about the December 2025 coup attempt. Journalist Angela Kpeidja was [detained on 16 December 2025 over two Facebook posts](<https://mfwa.org/country-highlights/benin-prosecutor-seeks-two-year-prison-term-for-journalist-over-facebook-posts/>). CPJ says she [was sentenced to 12 months in prison](<https://cpj.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/EN-CPJ-Letter-to-His-Excellency-the-President-of-Benin-September-1-2026.pdf>). Nothing found says the internet was cut or a platform blocked. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

On 5 May 2026 the Higher Council for Communication [indefinitely suspended TV5 Monde broadcasts](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/military-authorities-continue-to-suspend-csos-including-largest-student-union/>). In the last twelve months, on 26 May 2026, the Minister of Territorial Administration [suspended UGEB for three months after its statement](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/military-authorities-continue-to-suspend-csos-including-largest-student-union/>) criticising the military authorities' security record. [The Ouagadougou prosecutor opened an investigation into its authors](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/military-authorities-continue-to-suspend-csos-including-largest-student-union/>). [The online platforms of RFI, France 24, Jeune Afrique and Le Monde, among others, remained inaccessible in Burkina Faso in 2024](<https://burkina24.com/2025/02/11/droits-numeriques-au-burkina-faso-le-centre-national-de-presse-norbert-zongo-presente-son-rapport-2024/>). Nothing found says whether anyone was arrested or jailed for speech. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

On 9 February 2026 [the chairperson of the civil society body BOCONGO told the minister](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/89903>) that the Constitutional Court process needs meaningful, inclusive participation. In July 2022 Tshepo Sethibe, director of Moeladilotlhoko News Boiler, [was charged with publishing “alarming information” on Facebook](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/82198>) over posts on the police handling of a disappearance. The state withdrew the charge in October 2024. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says whether anyone in Botswana was punished for speech in that time, and no cut or block has been found. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

No stage is set. Access Now [lists the Central African Republic among 15 African countries with an internet shutdown in 2025](<https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/resilience-and-resistance-internet-shutdowns-in-africa-in-2025/>), and ISS Africa [lists it among six in Central Africa that year](<https://issafrica.org/iss-today/internet-shutdowns-won-t-solve-central-africa-s-political-crises>). Neither gives a month or an order, so no cut is shown inside the last twelve months. A decree set up a government spokesperson's unit to counter rumours, [a communications monitoring unit](<https://www.alwihdainfo.com/centrafrique-le-gouvernement-se-dote-dune-cellule-de-veille-communicationnelle-pour-contrer-les-rumeurs/>). Nothing found says government policy is criticised in public inside the country, or that anyone was punished for what they said. Absent would need a dated cut or block inside the past twelve months.

On 3 September 2025 the opposition party PPA-CI [publicly denounced the arrest of one of its activists](<https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20250903-c%C3%B4te-d-ivoire-un-cyberactiviste-interpell%C3%A9-apr%C3%A8s-avoir-%C3%A9voqu%C3%A9-les-d%C3%A9lib%C3%A9rations-du-conseil-constitutionnel>) as a violation of freedom of expression. The activist, Mamadou Zigui, was arrested on 2 September 2025 over a social-media video. RFI also reports that on 30 June 2025 the Abidjan court sentenced activist Gala Kolebi to 18 months for spreading false news. The prosecutor says a nurse [received 36 months and a 5 million fine on 18 July 2025](<https://www.afriksoir.net/cote-divoire-diakite-moussa-auteur-menaces-contre-opposition-defere-le-procureur-met-en-garde/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing found says the internet was cut. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

OONI's measurements suggest Cameroon [blocked TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and Telegram from 31 October to 5 November 2025](<https://explorer.ooni.org/findings/2025-cameroon-blocked-social-media-amid-post-election-protests>), during post-election protests. Access Now's #KeepItOn report [counts four internet shutdowns in Cameroon in 2025](<https://www.accessnow.org/internet-shutdowns-2025/>). In the last twelve months, on 8 and 9 June 2026, Civic Watch Cameroon's head and others met at [a workshop in Yaounde on the 2010 cybercrime law](<https://lejour.cm/cameroun-quand-les-lois-sur-la-cybercriminalite-menacent-les-libertes/>). They said it limits free expression. Nothing found names who ordered the 2025 blocks, and no source says the government is barred from such cuts. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

In October 2026 Fidèle Mbilizi Mutimanwa of the indigenous peoples' league LINAPYCO [criticised the state for leaving the Commission's 2022 Batwa decision and law 22/030 largely unapplied](<https://ishr.ch/latest-updates/achpr89-side-event-protecting-our-land-our-environment-and-digital-space-in-africa/>). In the last twelve months, the Committee to Protect Journalists says, journalist Tresor Muntu was [detained on 15 September 2026 and charged with defamation and publishing false news](<https://cpj.org/2026/09/drc-journalist-detained-prosecuted-for-sharing-x-post-on-whatsapp/>). OLPA says [the main mobile networks in Fizi have been cut since July 2026](<https://www.opinion-info.cd/societe/2026/09/21/rdc-lolpa-alerte-sur-la-multiplication-des-atteintes-la-liberte-de-la-presse-et>). No source names who ordered the cuts in Fizi or at Goma. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

On 15 March 2026, the day of the presidential election, NetBlocks [recorded a nation-scale shutdown of the internet in Congo](<https://www.telecoms.com/telecoms-law/internet-goes-down-in-congo-in-time-for-the-election>). ISS Africa [calls it an ad hoc shutdown during the polls](<https://issafrica.org/iss-today/internet-shutdowns-won-t-solve-central-africa-s-political-crises>). It says the government's reasons do not appear to meet the UN's tests of legality and necessity. In the last twelve months, police [arrested the human rights defender Ghislain Ondele Kanga at his home on 30 May 2026](<https://www.fidh.org/fr/themes/defenseurs-des-droits-humains/congo-poursuite-du-harcelement-judiciaire-et-ouverture-du-proces-de-m-33088>). FIDH says he was charged with false dissemination and with declaring an unauthorised demonstration. Nothing found names the authority that ordered the March 2026 shutdown, or says when it ended. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

[Mayotte Hebdo says police arrested Al-Watwan correspondent Abdou Moustoifa on 17 November 2025 over a Facebook post](<https://www.mayottehebdo.com/actualite/societe/comores-une-journaliste-entendue-par-la-police-a-cause-dun-post-facebook/>) about migrants held in a Moroni police station. In the last twelve months, in December 2025, the Comorian press [mobilised against a ministry and CNPA proposal to amend article 169 of the Information Code on source protection](<https://www.mayottehebdo.com/actualite/societe/comores-une-journaliste-entendue-par-la-police-a-cause-dun-post-facebook/>). The draft would have let a judge compel journalists to reveal sources, and MPs rejected it on 26 December 2025. [Article 361 of the penal code makes defamation a criminal offence](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/UNESCO_org_UPR46_COM_E_Main.pdf>). Nothing found says the internet was cut or a service blocked. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

[On 10 November 2026 the opposition party UCID questioned the government's digital transition](<https://www.inforpress.cv/en/parlamento-ucid-alerta-para-riscos-da-digitalizacao-nas-micro-pequenas-e-medias-empresas>). Its deputy Zilda Oliveira feared a higher tax burden on small firms. [In August 2025 the RECADDH human-rights network denounced prosecutions and intimidation of journalists](<https://www.balai.cv/noticias/recaddh-contra-escalada-de-perseguicoes-judiciais-e-ataques-a-jornalistas-em-cabo-verde/>) and called for the cases to be dropped. It named two journalists accused of qualified disobedience over reports on a death, Herminio Silves and Daniel Almeida. Nothing found says whether anyone was punished for speech in the last twelve months, and no cut or block has been found. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

The US State Department's 2024 human rights report says [the government owned the only radio and television stations](<https://dj.usembassy.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/165/2025/08/624521_DJIBOUTI-2024-HUMAN-RIGHTS-REPORT-1.pdf>). It says the newspaper La Nation held a monopoly on authorized print media. It adds that official media generally did not criticise government policy. In the last twelve months, exiled journalist Zineb Haddaji told CIVICUS Lens in July 2026 that [opposition and exiled media websites are blocked in Djibouti](<https://lens.civicus.org/interview/djibouti-silence-is-the-mechanism-that-makes-authoritarianism-possible/>). The opposition party RADDE says [police arrested a journalist and a cameraman of its citizens' rights programme on 20 November 2025](<https://en.kaabtv.com/djibouti-opposition-condemns-arbitrary-arrest-of-journalist-and-cameraman/>). Nothing found says a newspaper, broadcaster, party or group inside Djibouti criticised government policy in public in the last three years. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

No stage is set. Amnesty International says [seven journalists and media workers were detained, prosecuted or convicted from November 2025](<https://www.aialgerie.org/2026/05/13/algerie-les-autorites-doivent-liberer-les-journalistes-detenus-arbitrairement-et-respecter-la-liberte-de-la-presse/>) over their work or opinions. On 7 July 2026 the Algiers appeal court [upheld journalist Saad Bouakba's conviction over statements on historical events](<https://www.cfjustice.org/fr/algerie-committee-for-justice-la-condamnation-en-appel-du-journaliste-saad-bouakba-et-la-fermeture-du-media-rassd-aggravent-la-censure-du-debat-public/>). In the last twelve months, from 7 June 2026, [Algeria confined its exam shutdown measures to the inside of exam centres](<https://www.accessnow.org/noexamshutdown-one-step-forward-another-step-back/>). On 15 June 2025, the first day of the baccalaureate, [Facebook and TikTok were blocked in Algeria](<https://www.tsa-algerie.com/bac-2025-en-algerie-pas-de-blocage-total-dinternet-une-premiere/>). Nothing found says a paper, broadcaster, party or group inside the country criticised a government policy in public. Preparing would need a dated source showing such criticism, and no cut in the past twelve months.

In February 2026 Access Now and other groups said [the authorities were still blocking independent media sites, at least 630 websites in all](<https://www.accessnow.org/press-release/human-rights-abuses-facilitated-by-applogic-networks-in-egypt/>). In November 2026 CPJ said [the site of the outlet Zawia3 is blocked inside Egypt](<https://cpj.org/2026/11/how-egypts-laws-are-used-to-choke-its-independent-press/>). In the last twelve months, on 27 October 2026, a Cairo court [fined Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah EGP 3 million and ordered the news website closed](<https://manassa.news/en/news/34822>). Human Rights Watch says security forces [arrested the six journalists of the Matsda2sh newsroom on 28 and 29 September 2026](<https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/02/egypt-authorities-arrest-entire-investigative-newsroom>). On 10 November 2026 the UN human rights office said [they remained in detention](<https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/11/1168778>). No bar on cuts or blocks has been found. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

UNESCO states, in a document dated January 2026, that the Ministry of Information [runs all television, radio and newspapers in Eritrea](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/UNESCO_org_UPR46_ERI_E_Main.pdf>). It states that [privately owned outlets effectively ceased to exist after a government ban in 2001](<https://upr-info.org/sites/default/files/country-document/2026-01/UNESCO_org_UPR46_ERI_E_Main.pdf>). It presents that position as continuing. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No outlet independent of the state has been found carrying public criticism. Nothing found says whether anyone in Eritrea has been cut off, arrested or charged for speech. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

On 2 November 2026 the Ethiopian Media Authority [suspended the registration of The Reporter's publisher indefinitely](<https://cpj.org/2026/11/ethiopia-suspends-the-reporter-indefinitely-in-escalating-assault-on-independent-media/>). It said the paper's reports undermine national interests. On 31 October 2026 The Reporter had [published an editorial, 'Press Freedom Is Not A Luxury!'](<https://cpj.org/2026/11/ethiopia-suspends-the-reporter-indefinitely-in-escalating-assault-on-independent-media/>), criticising the authorities for treating independent reporting as a threat to national security. In the last twelve months, Amnesty International says, Addis Standard's managing editor, Million Beyene, was [abducted by intelligence agents on 15 April 2026](<https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2026/05/east-and-southern-africa-media-freedom-under-attack-amid-prevailing-impunity/>) and held for two weeks. In October 2026 Access Now reported [new internet shutdowns in Tigray](<https://www.accessnow.org/indefinite-internet-shutdowns/>). No source names who ordered the 2026 outages in Tigray and Amhara. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

[The HAC lifted the suspension, ordered on 17 February 2026, on 24 October 2026](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-la-hac-leve-la-suspension-des-reseaux-sociaux/>), citing cooperation with TikTok, Meta and YouTube. The regulator had suspended social media in Gabon by [decision no. 0002/HAC/2026, until further notice](<https://www.gabonreview.com/gabon-cinq-mois-de-silence-numerique-quand-le-remede-devient-le-poison/>). On 10 August 2026 the HAC [suspended the news site Info241 until further notice](<https://cpj.org/2026/08/gabons-online-news-outlet-info241-suspended-for-publishing-allegations-about-president/>). Activist Bob Mengome was [arrested on 19 January 2026 and charged with defamation](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/restrictive-regulation-on-social-media-use-adopted-amid-ongoing-suspension-of-social-media-platforms/>) over a voice message criticising the president. In the last twelve months, nine civil-society organisations [met in Libreville on 11 July 2026 and called the suspension unconstitutional and disproportionate](<https://www.gabonreview.com/gabon-cinq-mois-de-silence-numerique-quand-le-remede-devient-le-poison/>). No bar on such cuts has been found. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

On 13 September 2026 senior nursing officer Salomey Awiti Bafoh was [arrested and charged with abetment of publishing false news](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/barker-vormawor-urges-courts-to-scrutinise-rights-violations-in-ghana-jollof-case/>). She [pleaded not guilty and was remanded without bail](<https://www.myjoyonline.com/barker-vormawor-urges-courts-to-scrutinise-rights-violations-in-ghana-jollof-case/>). On 13 April 2026 police [arrested opposition figures Kwame Baffoe and Abubakar Yakubu over online publications](<https://demo.mfwa.org/issues-in-focus/mfwa-decries-wanton-and-discriminatory-use-of-false-news-laws/>). MFWA [counted 14 arrests under the false-news laws in the 16 months from 7 January 2025](<https://demo.mfwa.org/issues-in-focus/mfwa-decries-wanton-and-discriminatory-use-of-false-news-laws/>). On 7 November 2026 Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin [called for repeal of Section 208 of the Criminal Offences Act](<https://gna.org.gh/2026/11/afenyo-markin-calls-for-repeal-of-section-208-of-criminal-offences-act/>), the false-news offence. No cut or block has been found in the last twelve months. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

On 17 September 2026 the HAC [ordered the telecoms regulator ARPT to block all France 24 digital access points](<https://www.africaguinee.com/la-chaine-france-24-interdite-de-diffusion-en-guinee-larpt-et-canal-requisitionnes-par-la-hac/>). The same day it [revoked the national broadcasting authorisation of France 24 and withdrew its correspondents accreditations](<https://www.africaguinee.com/la-chaine-france-24-interdite-de-diffusion-en-guinee-larpt-et-canal-requisitionnes-par-la-hac/>). In the last twelve months, Facebook, YouTube and TikTok were [blocked from 28 July 2026, according to the bloggers association ABLOGUI](<https://www.guinee360.com/28/07/2026/perturbation-de-lacces-a-internet-en-guinee-lablogui-denonce-un-blocage-cible-de-facebook-youtube-et-tiktok/>). On 4 August 2026 the Union pour la defense des consommateurs [denounced the social media restrictions as a state decision harming the right to information](<https://www.guinee114.com/2026/08/04/guinee-bany-sidibe-denonce-les-restrictions-sur-les-reseaux-sociaux-et-la-degradation-de-linternet/>). No source says who ordered the July 2026 restrictions, or when they ended. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

On 24 March 2025 the National Assembly [passed the Criminal Offence and Procedure Bill 2025](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/new-criminal-law-and-draft-cybercrime-bill-in-the-gambia-threatens-press-freedom-freedom-of-expression-and-digital-rights/>). It [dropped the offences of criminal defamation and sedition](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/new-criminal-law-and-draft-cybercrime-bill-in-the-gambia-threatens-press-freedom-freedom-of-expression-and-digital-rights/>). In the last twelve months, on 14 May 2026, the Gambia Press Union [called the Cybercrime Bill 2023, the Communications Bill 2025 and the Criminal Offences Act 2025 threats to media freedom](<https://gambiaj.com/society/human-rights/gpu-warns-press-freedom-gains-mask-growing-threats-against-journalists-in-the-gambia/>). It said that [the Supreme Court had struck down criminal defamation and false publication online](<https://gambiaj.com/society/human-rights/gpu-warns-press-freedom-gains-mask-growing-threats-against-journalists-in-the-gambia/>), with no date for the ruling. In October 2024 the High Court [charged The Voice's editor and a reporter with false publication](<https://monitor.civicus.org/explore/new-criminal-law-and-draft-cybercrime-bill-in-the-gambia-threatens-press-freedom-freedom-of-expression-and-digital-rights/>). Nothing found says the last twelve months passed with no one punished for speech. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

On 26 November 2025 [citizens reported widespread restrictions on Facebook, YouTube, TikTok and Instagram](<https://mfwa.org/country-highlights/guinea-bissau-military-takeover-triggers-media-suspension-online-restrictions/>). The Media Foundation for West Africa says [the military imposed them](<https://mfwa.org/country-highlights/guinea-bissau-military-takeover-triggers-media-suspension-online-restrictions/>). The source gives no end date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found reports public criticism of government policy, or a person punished for speech. No source found names a bar on such cuts. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

Access Now says the island of Annobón [has had no internet or phone service since July 2024](<https://www.ambolegadu.com/en/annobon-sin-internet-access-now-reune-testimonios-y-reclama-el-fin-del-apagon/>). It puts the blackout down to the government. Its report of 20 October 2026 [lists Annobón among places under indefinite blackouts](<https://www.accessnow.org/indefinite-internet-shutdowns/>). In the last twelve months, AFP reported on 16 September 2026 that [the author of a viral video accusing the vice-president of corruption was arrested by the authorities](<https://www.seneweb.com/fr/news/Afrique/guinee-equatoriale-coupure-de-facebook-et-tiktok_n_504430.html>). [Ley 7/2024 on social networks and cybercrime](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/ley_por_la_que_se_regula_el_uso_de_las_redes_sociales_los_delitos_informaticos_y_la_ciber_delincuencia>) is [in full force, the government said on 1 July 2026](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_gobierno_recuerda_la_plena_vigencia_de_la_ley_que_regula_el_uso_de_las_redes_sociales_los_delitos_informaticos_y_la_ciber_delincuencia>). Nothing found says a paper, party or group inside the country criticised a government policy in public. Preparing would need public criticism of a government policy from inside the country, and no cut in the past twelve months.

In March 2026 the Court of Appeal [struck down two sections of the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act on false publication](<https://www.southernafricalitigationcentre.org/oral-statement-under-item-3-the-human-rights-situation-in-africa/>). The sections [carried fines up to KSh 5 million](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/kenya-le-parlement-veut-retablir-les-sanctions-contre-les-fausses-informations-en-ligne>), and the National Assembly has [appealed to the Supreme Court](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/kenya-le-parlement-veut-retablir-les-sanctions-contre-les-fausses-informations-en-ligne>). In the last twelve months, on 25 February 2026, journalist Peter Mwita [was charged under the Act over a WhatsApp message](<https://cpj.org/2026/02/kenya-court-due-to-rule-on-cybercrimes-law-as-another-journalist-faces-jail/>). Access Now [counts three internet shutdowns in Kenya in 2025](<https://www.accessnow.org/internet-shutdowns-2025/>). [OONI recorded a same-day block of Telegram Web on 25 June 2025](<https://explorer.ooni.org/findings/2025-kenya-blocks-access-to-telegram-amid-anti-government-protes>). No law or court ruling barring cuts has been found. Establishing would need twelve months with no arrest, charge, jailing, suspension or closure for speech.

In September 2026 [police arrested Jerry Nyanti Wratto in Monrovia, charged him and sent him to court under the Cybercrime Act](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202609240628.html>) over Facebook and TikTok posts about the Vice President. [The Vice President asked for his release](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/koung-seeks-release-of-ai-image-suspect/>), and [no court outcome is given](<https://frontpageafricaonline.com/liberias-cybercrime-law-faces-its-first-real-trial-as-vp-koung-case-exposes-liberias-widening-fault-lines/>). On 24 September 2026 [the Cybercrime Act's provisions on false information and offensive communication were called vague and a weapon to silence critics](<https://allafrica.com/stories/202609240628.html>). The critics were the Press Union of Liberia and civil society groups. In October 2026 the Press Union [called for the withdrawal of a confidentiality agreement for civil servants](<https://liberiapublicradio.com/2026/10/24/pul-condemns-governments-assault-on-freedom-of-information-and-transparency-calls-for-immediate-withdrawal-of-confidentiality-policy-undermining-the-foi-act/>).
